citation: Frank Morley Woodruff, The Birds of the Chicago Area. Bulletin No. VI of the Natural History Survey, The Chicago Academy of Sciences. Chicago: The Chicago Academy of Sciences, 1907.
author: Frank Morley Woodruff, curator, Chicago Academy of Sciences
describes_date: the birds of the Chicago area as the Academy's curator and its correspondents knew them in the years up to 1907, three years after the 1904 scene
repository: Internet Archive, from the University of California Biology Library copy (bequest of Theodore S. Palmer)
locator: Internet Archive item birdsofchicagoar00woodrich; text layer birdsofchicagoar00woodrich_djvu.txt, 581,329 bytes, sha256 0d94e430baa63a0afaec50437758d262d1919322c71c6956e5adbd7f25b019b4. American Robin, Merula migratoria, p. 195: 'The American Robin is an abundant summer resident, arriving early in April, and departing in October.' The introduction, p. 14, on feeding birds round the author's house in winter: 'Even the imported sparrows freeze in their warm nests.' The species list has no entry for the European starling (the only Sturnus in it is the meadowlark's old name, Sturnus ludovicianus).
rights_note: Published 1907 and out of copyright in the United States.
access_notes: Located through the Internet Archive search API and its text layer downloaded in full on 2026-11-13 for T-3585; the sha256 above is of that download. The robin account and the p. 14 sentence were read in the OCR text, which reads cleanly for these passages.
what_it_supplies: The American robin as an abundant summer resident of the Chicago area, arriving early in April and departing in October, in the decade of the 1904 scene.
The imported (house) sparrow already established round Chicago houses by 1907.
No European starling in the Chicago list of 1907.
what_it_does_not_supply: A robin observed on Prairie Avenue or on any particular day of 1904.
Singing hours, song rate or the number of birds on a street.
Any identification of the project's robin recording, which is a modern Spokane proxy.
note: Cited by the 1904 parkway robin placements in assets/audio/intake.json (T-3585), with the modern Illinois DNR account for residential habitat.
